title: MCP servers
summary: Give every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Kilo Code, OpenRouter and LiteLLM) extra tools by registering MCP servers. One switch per agent, Approve MCP servers, decides who receives them; JayV hands the servers over on every request, each agent in the way it understands. OpenRouter and LiteLLM have no tools of their own, so JayV calls the MCP tools for them.
usage: Open Settings › MCP (or Ctrl+K › Settings › MCP) and add a server by form, or paste a configuration (mcpServers JSON, a claude mcp add line or an npx command). In a chat, type /mcp followed by a configuration or a description: an agent drafts the configuration and nothing is saved until you review it and click Save settings. Four official servers (sequential-thinking, fetch, git and memory) come registered, as entries you can turn off, edit or remove; fetch and git run through uvx, so uv must be installed. Turning a server on or off, editing, adding or removing it takes effect only when you click Save settings; Discard drops the change. Servers of an organization are not listed here but under MCP in that organization’s environment; in its chats (the general one and each project’s) they win over yours with the same name, even when the organization turns one off. Then turn on Approve MCP servers in the Settings tab of each agent that should use them (it starts off); Ctrl+K › Approve MCP servers does the same for one agent. Organizations can block it per agent, and planning mode never carries the servers.
